# reflex-kernel

A browser workbench built with [Reflex](https://reflex.dev), in the spirit of
`experimental/textual-kernel`: chat with the Smash agent (`ds.ai.agent`) across the top; below
it, everything its tools return shows up as a tab named `r1`, `r2`, … (tables as sortable, filterable
grids, match videos as a playable gallery, other results as a field list), side by side with
Jupyter-style Python cells where those names are plain Python objects (tables are polars DataFrames).
Drag the chat strip's or the tables pane's bottom-right corner to resize them. The bottom bar shows or hides each pane.

```sh
cd experimental/reflex-kernel
uv run reflex run
# -> http://localhost:3000
```

Design intent lives in `spec/experimental/reflex-kernel/`: navigation, keys and much of the look follow
Omarchy (`spec/experimental/reflex-kernel/omarchy.md`).

## SmashGPT (desktop app)

On Omarchy this app is **SmashGPT**: `SUPER+SHIFT+I` opens it in its own web app window, or focuses
the one already open (`.os/scripts/keybindings/smashgpt.sh`). The server runs as a systemd user
service, `~/.config/systemd/user/smashgpt.service`, started at login by `~/.config/hypr/autostart.lua`;
if it isn't up, the shortcut starts it and opens the window once it answers (cold start up to about
a minute). It's also in the app launcher as the SmashGPT web app. All of this is tracked by `os sync`.

```sh
systemctl --user restart smashgpt      # eg after changing dependencies
journalctl --user -u smashgpt -f       # server logs
.os/scripts/keybindings/smashgpt.sh status
```

The service runs `reflex run` in dev mode, so code edits hot-reload in the open window. Stop it
before running the app by hand (both use ports 3000 and 8000).

Runs from the repo's root venv (no own `pyproject.toml`); needs the AI Gateway key the rest of
`ds.ai` uses.

- **Chat**: Enter sends, Shift+Enter adds a line. Tool calls are listed above each reply.
  Hover a message for its copy button on the top-right corner (a reply copies as its markdown source).
  A failed turn (the model or a tool raised) shows its traceback in the same component a Python cell uses
  (`render.traceback_view`): the frame that raised and the error, the rest folded, and a copy button (top right,
  on hover) that copies the full plain-text traceback.
  Each tool result gets a row (`r1 · tool · 10 videos`): click it to unfold the result inline (grid,
  gallery, fields; folded by default), or `open →` to open it as a tab in Results.
- **Debug log** (bug icon in the title bar, `Alt+D`): every outside call the app made, newest first:
  start.gg GraphQL requests (operation, page, status, time, start.gg's object count), other HTTP fetches
  (supermajor search, smash-tube), agent turns (time, tool calls, tokens) and tool steps. A row unfolds to its
  details: the request as sent (method, url, headers with secrets filtered, body or GraphQL query and
  variables), the response (status, type, size, `cf-ray`, the start of an error body), page info, timing
  (including the wait for start.gg's rate budget), the lookup's `group`, session, origin
  (`chat` / `form` / `view` / `cell`) and error. Copy buttons give the record as JSON and the request as a curl
  command (secrets as `$AUTHORIZATION` / `$APIKEY`, set them before running it). A row's `↖` link goes to
  where it came from, with the same scroll-and-flash as Show in Chat (`State.reveal`, `window.reveal` in
  `assets/panes.js`, the app's one way of navigating): the tool call's row in the chat (records made during a
  tool call carry its `tool_call_id`, from `ds.ai.call_log.ToolCallLog`), the chat turn, the result tab whose
  form ran it, or the cell. The other way round, the bug on a tool call or your message in the chat, or on a
  cell (on hover), or Show Requests in a result tab's right-click menu, opens the log on just that thing's
  requests (`State.show_logs`, `logs.in_focus`; the same target ids as the links). On top:
  start.gg requests in the last 60 s against the 80 allowed, the backend's memory, and this session's variables
  (count, rough size). Filter by kind or to this session; Clear forgets them. Records come from
  `ds.util.http` / `ds.util.graphql` and are kept in memory only (`reflex_kernel/logs.py`, newest 2000, gone on restart);
  the panel loads them when opened, on Refresh and when a turn, form or cell finishes, never while closed.
  A new kind of record is one function in `logs.LOG_FORMATS`.
- **Tables**: click a tab to switch, type in the filter box to search. Click a column header to sort
  (ascending, descending, unsorted); filter and sort work the same in a tab and in a cell's result.
  The grid shows at most 2000 rows; the DataFrame itself is never truncated.
- **Widgets are data-driven** (`reflex_kernel/widgets.py`): every kind of view is a row in `WIDGETS`, and the
  app reads a widget's behaviour from that row instead of hard-coding it per widget:

  | attribute | meaning |
  | --- | --- |
  | `kind`, `title` | the view kind `render.py` draws, and its name for people |
  | `tool`, `hide` | the agent tool it mimics: gives it a tool form (below); `hide` = parameters not on the form |
  | `new` | for a widget that is no tool's result: the blank value `+` binds (eg a SmashDb console) |
  | `addable` | offered in the Results tab bar's `+` menu, to add by hand (needs `tool` or `new`) |
  | `chat_open` | starts unfolded in the chat when the agent returns it (others start as a folded row) |

  Today: `table`, `videos` (`find_match_videos`, addable), `usage` (`get_player_usage`, addable, unfolded in
  chat), `fields`, `smashdb` (the SmashDb console, addable), `tool`. A new attribute is a field on `Widget` plus the one place that reads it. A new widget
  is a row, a `case` in `render.to_view`, and its component in `render.render_component`.
- **Links look like links, in every widget**: text that opens a url is drawn with `render.link(text, href)`:
  blue and underlined, exactly as a link in the agent's markdown reply (`.md a, a.link` in `assets/app.css`),
  opening in a new tab. Don't style a hyperlink as plain text, and don't give a widget its own link style.
  The one other form is a link drawn as a button (the video player's `YouTube ↗`, class `act`).
- **Player usage** (kind `usage`, `ds.data.startgg.PlayerUsage`, built from start.gg sets; it replaced the
  supermajor.gg version when that site began blocking automated clients): a player at a glance. Its form has
  `player`, `vs character` (only games against that character), `months` and `setting`. An All / Offline /
  Online toggle at the top picks which events the whole view counts; it runs the tool again with that
  `setting` (a few seconds the first time, since offline-only reaches further back than the capped mix), and
  each recent event carries an `offline` (filled) or `online` (outlined) tag and its name is a link to the
  event's start.gg page. Characters as ranked bars with
  their stock icons (switch between all games, game 1 and events), one line on how often they change
  character within a set, stages in three groups (starters, counterpicks, taken to; often empty, since many
  brackets report no stages), and the characters played at each recent event as icons (hover for games). The
  tab's note gives the real date span and the set / game counts. No results are shown. Past 6 rows the tail folds
  into one "N others" row; hover a row for the count. Bars rather than a pie: lengths on one baseline compare
  close shares exactly, and the icons, not colours, say which character. The icons are
  `pkgs/ds/data/char_icons/` (`ds.data.char_icon_by_name`), served by the backend (`api.py`).
- **Tool forms** (`reflex_kernel/tool_forms.py`): some results show the inputs of the agent tool that made
  them. `Inputs ▸` in their bar folds them open, filled with what the tool was called with; change them and
  press Enter (or Run) to run the tool again in place. The `+` at the end of the Results tab bar, or `Alt+P` anywhere
  (`Shortcut.ADD_WIDGET`: the same menu in the middle of the window; it has a search box, so type to filter, arrows and Enter pick, `Alt+P` or Esc
  closes), adds one
  by hand: a placeholder (`ToolRequest`) that is just the form, replaced by the result on its first run.
  How the form stays aligned with the tool:
  - **Fields** are built from the tool's parameter schema, the one pydantic-ai gives the model
    (`schema_fields`: names, types, defaults, descriptions; a `Literal` becomes a dropdown). Nothing about a
    tool's parameters is written a second time.
  - **The type decides the input, not the name**, so any tool gets the same one:

    | type hint | input |
    | --- | --- |
    | `str` | text box |
    | `int` / `float` | number box |
    | `bool` | checkbox |
    | `Literal[...]` / `Enum` | dropdown |
    | `CharEnum` (eg `CharGroup`) | choice input, one pick |
    | `list[CharGroup]`, `list[Literal[...]]`, `list[SomeEnum]` | choice input, several picks |
    | `list[str]` | text box (no options to pick from) |

    Conventions:
    - The choice input is one component, single or multiple (`render._choice_input`, `assets/choice.js`,
      `tool_forms.picker_for`): a box with a chip per pick (× removes it) that opens the list. The only
      difference: several picks tick and untick with the list kept open; one pick replaces the last.
    - A long list (over `CHOICE_SEARCH_AT`, 8 options, eg characters) gets a search box on top, single or
      multiple alike; a short one (eg `rounds`) doesn't.
    - `T | None` gets the same input as `T` for dropdowns and choice inputs. A plain `int | None` /
      `bool | None` gets a text box (its schema is an `anyOf` with no single `type`).
    - The parameter's default fills the input, and its docstring description is the tooltip.
    - An empty input means the default (`any` for choice inputs).
    - A choice input submits `a,b`, which `tool_forms.arguments` turns back into `T`'s values.
    - To change an input, change the type hint. The form code needs no edit (`ToolForm.fields`;
      tested in `tests/experimental/reflex_kernel/test_widgets.py`).
  - **Values** go through the validator pydantic-ai uses for the model's calls, then the same tool function.
  - **Which inputs made a result** is recorded by the session (`Session.calls`): the agent's tool-call
    arguments, or the form as run. Paging keeps them; a value made in Python has none (an empty form).
    The form shows what the tool was called with (eg `player_1=Joker`), the bar what was really searched.
  - **Back to the original**: for a result the agent made, the session also keeps the agent's own call
    (`Call.original`: its inputs and result). Once the form is re-run, `Inputs` turns green and an × in
    the form puts both back, without fetching again (`Session.restore_original`). A form added by hand
    has no original.
  - `tests/experimental/reflex_kernel/test_tool_forms.py` checks every tool form; `test_widgets.py` the registry.

  Which widgets have one is `Widget.tool` in `widgets.py`; `_bar` adds the `Inputs` button to any view with
  a form, and the widget's component places `form_section` under its bar.
- **Table SQL** (as in DBeaver): `SQL ▸` in a table's bar unfolds a one-line SQL box under it, starting
  as `select * from self`. Ctrl+Enter (`Shortcut.RUN_SQL`) runs it on the table with polars' `df.sql`
  (PostgreSQL syntax, the table is `self`), and the grid shows the result, still filtered and sorted by
  the bar; `SQL` turns green while a query is applied, and × goes back to the whole table. A bad query
  shows its error and leaves the table as it was. The query is kept per view slot, like the filter
  (`Ui.sql`, `View.table`); the value bound to the name is never changed.
- **SmashDb console** (kind `smashdb`, `reflex_kernel/db_console.py`; `+` → SmashDb console): a small
  DataGrip. Left, the schema tree: every table with its row count; click one to unfold its columns and
  dtypes, `▶` (on hover) selects everything from it. Right, the query editor (the table SQL box's CodeMirror,
  completing every table and column): Ctrl+Enter (`Shortcut.RUN_SQL`) or Run runs it; with text selected only
  the selection runs, so several queries can sit in the box. Under it the result, which is the table widget
  itself (`render._table_bar` / `_table_body`): the same grid, header sort, row filter and `SQL ▸` on `self`
  as any DataFrame; the bar's note adds the time the query took. A failed query keeps the last result and
  shows its traceback in the component a Python cell and the chat use (`render.traceback_view`). `History ▸`
  lists this console's queries that ran (newest first, 20, each once); click one to put it back in the editor.
  - It queries the session's `db`, the one the Python cells have, so `create table x as select ...` in the
    console is there in a cell and the other way round (in memory only; the parquet files are never written).
  - The tab's name is bound to the console: `r3.df` is the result DataFrame, `r3.sql` its query.
  - Running a query makes a new `DbConsole` that replaces the old one at its slot, as a tool form's run does.
  - No cache: the tree is read from the db on every redraw (about 2 ms), so a new table shows at once.
- **Rendering** (`reflex_kernel/render.py`): everything about showing a value lives in this one file, used
  for agent tool results, cell outputs and tabs alike. Today: DataFrame / Series / list of pydantic models
  -> grid; `MatchVideos` (the agent's `find_match_videos`, smash-tube.com) -> thumbnail gallery; any other
  pydantic model -> its fields, with lists of models as small tables; `DbConsole` -> the SmashDb console;
  everything else -> its repr.
  It is two matches, because Reflex compiles components ahead of time and the browser never sees the
  Python object: `to_view(value)` is a Python `match` on the value's type (run when a cell or tool
  returns), and `render_component(view)` picks the component for the view's kind. To add a type, add a
  `case` to `to_view`; a new kind of view also needs a `case` (and its component) in `render_component`.
  **Design rule: a value renders as one contained component, the same wherever it is placed** (a tab,
  a cell output, later a popup or anything else). Everything that belongs to the view is inside what
  `render_component` returns: a table's filter and sort, a video list's player and paging. Its state
  (filter text, sort, picked video, folded list) travels in its `ViewData`, and the session keeps it
  per *slot*, the place a view is shown (`tab:<name>`, `chat:<name>` for a result unfolded in the chat, `cell:<id>`), so a view is back as it was left.
  Every interaction comes back through one handler, `State.view_event(slot, action, arg)`. A host only
  does `render_component(view, State.view_event)`: it adds nothing of the view's own around it, and
  `compact=True` changes sizing only. To show a view somewhere new, give that place a slot prefix
  (`Session.view_at` / `put`, `State._show`) and call `render_component`; no component logic is repeated.
- **Result tabs**: the x on a tab (or right-click: Close, Close Others, Close to the Right, Close All, as
  in VS Code) closes it. Only the tab goes: the name stays in Python, and the tab comes back when the name is
  bound to something new or the result is opened again from the chat (`Session.closed` / `tabs()`).
  A result the agent returned has `↖ chat` in its bar (and Show in Chat in the right-click menu): it
  scrolls the chat to that tool call's row and flashes it.
- **Help**: the ? at the top right (Alt+H) lists the keyboard shortcuts.
- **Keybindings**: Alt+K opens a searchable list of every shortcut, like Omarchy's SUPER+K: type to filter,
  Esc (or Alt+K) closes (`keys_palette`, `assets/keys.js`).
- **Floating a view**: every view (a tab, a cell's result, a result unfolded in the chat) has a button at
  its top right that floats it over the page, nearly full screen; click it again, press Esc or click
  outside to put it back. It is the same component, only restyled in the browser (`.is-floating`,
  `assets/panes.js`), so its sort, filter and playing video carry on.
- **Keyboard shortcuts** are all defined once, in `reflex_kernel/shortcuts.py`, as the `Shortcut` enum named
  by what they do (`Shortcut.FULL_SCREEN`, `Shortcut.RUN`, …). The help panel, tooltips, the cell editor's
  keymap (`codemirror_keys`) and `assets/panes.js` (`window.SHORTCUTS`) all read it: change a key there only.
- **Panes**: the bottom bar toggles Chat, Results (Alt+R) and Python (Alt+J, J for Jupyter; Alt+P is the add-widget menu), as in Zed. (Neither letter follows
  Omarchy, where `SUPER+P` / `SUPER+J` are window layout actions with nothing comparable here.) Only the chat
  shows at first (results also unfold inline in it, and `open →` brings up Results); a pane
  whose neighbour is hidden takes the freed space. Hidden cells keep their text.
- **Full screen**: each pane has a button with two diagonal arrows (top right) that fills the window
  with that pane; click it again to restore. Alt+F (`Shortcut.FULL_SCREEN`) floats the view you are in
  (see Floating a view), or, outside a view, fills the window with your pane: "you are in" is where
  keyboard focus is, else what you last clicked (`assets/panes.js`). The bottom-bar toggles
  keep their state while a pane is full screen; clicking one leaves full screen and shows that pane.
- **Match videos**: one component, the list plus the video picked from it. Click a card to play it:
  the list folds away so the video fills the component, and "Show list" in the player's bar brings it
  back under the player. It works the same in a tab and in a cell's result, each with its own picked
  video. Leaving a tab stops its video; it is back, paused, when you return. Prev / Next fetch the search's other
  pages. Videos whose uploader disabled embedding show YouTube's own message; use the "YouTube ↗" button.
- **Python cells**: Jupyter-style, each a CodeMirror editor with Everforest syntax colors.
  Shift+Enter runs a cell and moves to the next (adding one after the last), Ctrl+Enter runs in
  place, Tab indents. `pl` (polars) and `db` (`ds.data.SmashDb`) are predefined. A cell ending in a
  DataFrame (polars or pandas, or a Series) shows it in a compact version of the tables-pane grid (8 rows visible, columns sized
  to content, each header showing its polars dtype in italics on a second line, like polars' own notebook
  view; click a header to sort);
  "Open as tab" moves it up there as `out<n>`. Any value with a view (see Rendering) that you bind to a name becomes a tab. Variables persist until the server restarts.
- **Completion**: pops up as you type. Tab accepts the highlighted suggestion (Enter also works), or
  opens the list after a name or a dot; elsewhere Tab indents. Ctrl+Space forces the list. Suggestions come from `jedi` run
  against the live variables, so `r1.` lists real DataFrame methods. `jedi` is present in the root
  venv only as a dependency of IPython; add it to the root `pyproject.toml` if that changes.
- **Local only**: the backend binds to 127.0.0.1, since the app executes arbitrary Python.

Layout: `reflex_kernel/session.py` (namespace, agent, completion; no UI), `render.py` (Python value -> view -> component), `state.py` (Reflex
state), `reflex_kernel.py` (components), `editor.py` + `cell_editor.jsx` (CodeMirror wrapper),
`api.py` (`POST /complete`), `assets/app.css` (Everforest). Design mockups this came from:
`experimental/design_poc` (`/split`).
